business_problem: SBB needed real-time visibility into train cleanliness and yard locations so it could replace manual schedules and spreadsheets with operational decisions based on live rail data.
solution_summary: SBB built multiple railway-operations applications on MongoDB Atlas to turn train telemetry and staff updates into live operational workflows. In the Cleaning 4.0 project, train timetable information, distance traveled, passenger traffic, and other operational signals are collected and stored in Atlas, where they feed an analytical model that calculates the exact cleaning tasks required for each train. Those task lists are then synchronized to mobile devices used by cleaning crews via Atlas Device Sync and Atlas for the Edge. SBB used the same Atlas-centric pattern for its Gleisspiegel track-mirror application, where operators update engine and carriage locations from mobile apps and Atlas consolidates the data for other devices and web clients in real time. By combining mobile sync, cloud storage, and live operational analytics, SBB created a more resilient way to manage rail assets, cleaning, and maintenance without custom sync APIs.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Stores and distributes the operational rail data used by SBB's cleaning and yard-management applications.

solution_components.name: Atlas Device Sync
solution_components.role: Synchronizes operational updates between mobile devices, cloud data, and web applications in real time.

solution_components.name: Atlas for the Edge
solution_components.role: Supports the local mobile data layer used by cleaning crews and train operators in the field.

data_flow: Train timetable, distance, traffic, and location data flows into MongoDB Atlas, an analytical model derives cleaning tasks and asset states from that data, Atlas Device Sync pushes updates to mobile and web clients, and field staff feed new observations back into the same platform in real time.
business_outcome: SBB improved rail-operations efficiency, reduced the need for manual coordination, and created a mobile-first operational platform that supports faster cleaning, better yard visibility, and future analytics-driven optimization.
metrics: SBB spent billions cleaning and maintaining trains in 2022.
The cleaning app is planned to go live in 2024.
SBB reports that Atlas Device Sync can save months of development time.
architecture_clues: Cleaning 4.0 uses an analytical model driven by timetable, distance, and passenger-traffic data.
Atlas Device Sync provides bi-directional sync, compression in flight, and resilience to network interruptions.
The Gleisspiegel track-mirror app updates web clients using collection.watch() after mobile changes are synced.

“The output of the model is actually the cleaning task list, which is then synchronized with a mobile application that cleaners use to check their daily tasks.”
“Leveraging Atlas Device Sync, it becomes very easy to build and maintain new applications.”
“The precise, real-time location tracking enhances accessibility to train assets and increases efficiency of daily operations.”
